name: Motor Driven Cycle
description: A light motorcycle, moped or motor scooter. From January 1, 2027 it covers an electric motor rated above 750 W up to 8,000 W nominal, and every electric bicycle that isn't a Class 1, 2 or 3 low-speed electric bicycle, whatever its power.

restrictions.rule: A motorcycle, moped or motor scooter: a seat or saddle, and no more than three wheels on the ground
An electric motor rated above 750 W up to 8,000 W nominal, or a combustion engine under 150 cc
restrictions.citation: Illinois Vehicle Code §1-145.001, as amended by SB 3484 (2026)

restrictions.rule: The line is drawn only by engine displacement, which an electric motor doesn't have
Any electric bicycle that isn't a low-speed electric bicycle (pedals, a motor under 750 W, and Class 1, 2 or 3 limits) is a motor driven cycle, whatever its power
restrictions.citation: Illinois Vehicle Code §1-145.001, as amended by SB 3484 (2026)

restrictions.rule: Riders need a driver's license with a Class L (motor driven cycle) or Class M (motorcycle) classification
restrictions.citation: Illinois Vehicle Code §6-104; 92 Ill. Adm. Code 1030.30

restrictions.rule: Riders aged 16 or 17 may get an instruction permit to ride in daylight under the direct supervision of a licensed operator 21 or older with a year's experience
Rider and passenger must wear glasses, goggles or a face shield unless it has a windshield that rises above the rider's eyes; no helmet requirement
Titled and registered with the Secretary of State, carries a license plate, and must carry liability insurance
An electric one bought new must be titled if it has a VIN

It must have a VIN, meet federal motor vehicle safety standards and have a speedometer showing mph; one not built and equipped for highway use gets a distinctive title and can't be registered or ridden on public roads
restrictions.citation: Illinois Vehicle Code §11-1403.4, added by SB 3484 (2026)

restrictions.rule: Carries a passenger only if built for one, and a rider under 18 may carry only a sibling, stepsibling, child or stepchild
restrictions.citation: Illinois Vehicle Code §11-1403.4, added by SB 3484 (2026)

restrictions.rule: Barred from sidewalks, bike lanes, bicycle paths, shared-use paths, bike trails and interstate highways, and from public land where the agency in charge prohibits it; no local government may regulate it
restrictions.citation: Illinois Vehicle Code §11-1403.4, added by SB 3484 (2026)

restrictions.rule: Selling or advertising one as a device that isn't a motor driven cycle is consumer fraud, with a civil penalty of up to $10,000 per vehicle, and one ridden in violation may be impounded
restrictions.citation: Illinois Vehicle Code §11-1403.4, added by SB 3484 (2026)

restrictions.rule: The Department of Transportation may bar motor driven cycles from controlled access highways it signs
